Job Details

Yolk Digital is engaged by the Department of Home Affairs to provide an experienced Project Manager to plan and run ICT projects, owning day-to-day delivery across scope, schedule, budget, resourcing, risks and stakeholders.

You'll be accountable for hitting milestones and deliverables within time and budget, using the right methodology (Agile, Waterfall or hybrid) and heading off problems early with practical risk management and contingency plans. The work spans complex ICT environments, including IT service management, cybersecurity, enterprise software, infrastructure uplift and digital transformation.

You'll work with business stakeholders, sponsors, technical teams, vendors and end users, running workshops and decision-making forums and translating technical detail into clear communication for different audiences. You'll also support assurance, controls and compliance, oversee testing, user acceptance and deployment, and hand skills and documentation across to departmental staff so the capability stays with the department.

Location

ACT. Hybrid. You must work full time on site for the first 3 months, or until you understand the department's ICT landscape, requirements and project objectives. After that you must be on site in Canberra at least 3 days per week, subject to approval and the ICT Contractor Working from Home Guidelines. Remote work costs (for example travel, accommodation, utilities and equipment) are your own responsibility.

Duration

Commencing 2 November 2026, with the initial contract running to 30 June 2027 and 2 extension options of 12 months.

Citizenship

Australian Citizen

Clearance

Baseline

Key Responsibilities

* Manage project scope, schedule, budget, resourcing, risks, issues, procurement, stakeholder engagement, change control, governance and reporting
* Document a management plan that identifies the actions required to realise benefits
* Prepare timely, accurate and high-quality reports and project documents
* Lead and support the planning, coordination and delivery of ICT projects within complex environments
* Define project scope, objectives, deliverables, schedules, budgets and resource requirements
* Establish and maintain project governance, reporting and communication frameworks
* Engage and collaborate with business stakeholders, sponsors, technical teams, vendors and end users
* Facilitate workshops, meetings and decision-making forums to support project outcomes
* Coordinate project activities across multiple teams and service providers
* Monitor project progress, milestones, deliverables and dependencies
* Identify, assess and manage project risks, issues, changes and mitigation activities
* Maintain project documentation, risk registers, issue registers and status reports
* Develop, manage and monitor project budgets, expenditure and cost forecasts
* Ensure projects deliver value for money and achieve intended business benefits
* Support project assurance, controls, compliance and reporting activities
* Apply relevant government frameworks, standards and best practices to project delivery
* Translate technical information into clear and concise communications for diverse stakeholders
* Oversee testing, user acceptance, implementation and deployment activities
* Ensure solutions meet business requirements, technical standards and organisational policies
* Provide advice, analysis and recommendations to support informed decision-making and risk-based remediation
* Contribute to ICT initiatives, including IT service management, cybersecurity, enterprise software, infrastructure uplift and digital transformation projects
* Travel interstate as required
* Transfer skills and knowledge to departmental staff and store documentation in line with the Department's recordkeeping policy and practices

Skills & Experience

* Project management methodologies (Agile, Waterfall, Hybrid)
* IT infrastructure
* Business analysis and requirements management
* Testing assurance principles
* Vendor and contract management
* Leadership
* Communication and presentation
* Negotiation and influencing
* Problem-solving
* Conflict resolution
* Time management

Essential Criteria

1. Financial management: Level 4 (SFIA). Monitors and maintains financial records to agreed requirements for compliance and audit. Assists with identifying and calculating process, service, project and component costs for financial planning and budgeting. Collates required financial data and reports for analysis and to facilitate decision-making.
2. Organisational change management: Level 5 (SFIA). Develops the change management approach and a change management plan in collaboration with sponsors, users and project teams. Creates and implements action plans to ensure everything is ready for the change before going live. Acquires change management resources and develops their capabilities to deliver the required changes. Gathers feedback to allow timely improvements to the change management plan and approach. Assesses risks and takes preventative action. Develops and communicates tailored change management plans for senior stakeholder groups. Provides guidance and makes suggestions to support change sponsors.
3. Project management: Level 5 (SFIA). Takes full responsibility for the definition, approach, facilitation and satisfactory completion of medium-scale projects. Provides effective leadership to the project team. Adopts appropriate project management methods and tools. Manages the change control process and assesses and manages risks. Ensures that realistic project plans are maintained and delivers regular and accurate communication to stakeholders. Ensures project and product quality reviews occur on schedule and according to procedure. Ensures that project deliverables are completed within agreed cost, timescale and resource budgets, and are formally accepted, by appropriate stakeholders. Monitors costs, times, quality and resources used and takes action where performance deviates from agreed tolerances.
4. Requirements definition and management: Level 4 (SFIA). Defines and manages scoping, requirements definition and prioritisation activities for initiatives of medium size and complexity. Contributes to selecting the requirements approach. Facilitates input from stakeholders, provides constructive challenge and enables effective prioritisation of requirements. Establishes requirements base-lines, obtains formal agreement to requirements, and ensures traceability to source.
5. Stakeholder relationship management: Level 5 (SFIA). Identifies the communications and relationship needs of stakeholder groups. Translates communications/stakeholder engagement strategies into specific activities and deliverables. Facilitates open communication and discussion between stakeholders. Acts as a single point of contact by developing, maintaining and working to stakeholder engagement strategies and plans. Provides informed feedback to assess and promote understanding. Facilitates business decision-making processes. Captures and disseminates technical and business information.

Desirable Criteria

* Performance management: Level 4 (SFIA). Provides operational direction, support and guidance to assigned colleagues. Allocates routine tasks or project work, in line with team objectives and individual capabilities. Monitors quality and performance against agreed criteria to make learning recommendations or to escalate concerns. Coaches colleagues in developing target skills and capabilities in line with team and personal goals. Facilitates effective working relationships between team members.

Application Instructions

Upload a one page pitch addressing all criteria specified. This includes responding to the Job Details, Key Responsibilities, and Essential Criteria. The pitch cannot be more than 5000 characters.

How to write your pitch
* Use the STAR format for your strongest examples: Situation, Task, Action, Result. State the context, what you were accountable for, what you personally did, and the measurable outcome.
* Sell capability rather than listing duties. Show you have delivered projects within cost, time and resource budgets, not just that you managed them.
* Address each SFIA criterion by name and level: Financial management (4), Organisational change management (5), Project management (5), Requirements definition and management (4) and Stakeholder relationship management (5). Use the SFIA wording as your checklist.
* Show experience in complex ICT environments, with a mix of methodologies (Agile, Waterfall, hybrid) and with vendor and contract management.
* If you have led or coached team members, include it to speak to the desirable Performance management (Level 4) criterion.

If you have worked at the Department of Home Affairs before, include with your application the branch and division you worked in, your role and your dates.

new_jobs.title: Project Manager
new_jobs.description:
Young is a music and arts organisation, built around a London-based record label, that helps exceptional artists locate and develop their genius.

We are looking for an experienced, highly organised and culturally curious Project Manager to join the Young Recordings team and play a key role in bringing our artists’ campaigns to life.

Based at Young Space, our offices in East London, you will work closely with the General Manager, A&R, artists and their management from the earliest stages of a project, helping to shape campaign strategies and release plans that stay true to each artist’s creative vision. You will own the day-to-day delivery of assigned campaigns: translating strategy into action, coordinating teams across the label and the wider Beggars Group, and making sure every campaign is delivered thoughtfully, efficiently and to a high standard, in the UK and internationally.

The ideal candidate is someone who thrives being at the centre of things. They will be the trusted point person for artists, managers and internal teams alike, keeping timelines, assets and budgets on track while bringing together input from across creative, press, digital, marketing, radio, streaming, retail and international teams. They will be able to balance big-picture thinking with meticulous attention to detail, use sound judgement to solve problems as they arise, and bring genuine love and knowledge of music & culture to everything they do.

This is a full-time role, based 4 days per week in the office, with the option to work from home on Fridays.

EXPERIENCE:

At least 4 years of substantial, professional music or entertainment industry experience required

2+ years of demonstrated experience in product management or in a position managing day-to-day campaign logistics is required

Proven ability to take ownership of a diverse mix of artist campaigns from planning through execution, balancing strategic thinking with exceptional attention to detail

Strong understanding of the music industry and confidence working across multiple teams, stakeholders and international markets

Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build trusted relationships with key external and internal teams

Strong judgement, problem-solving skills and a proactive, solutions-oriented approach

Genuine cultural curiosity and a deep love and knowledge of music, with an understanding of Young’s creative identity and the wider Beggars Group

Highly organised, collaborative and able to manage multiple priorities in a fast-moving environment

A high level of discretion, professionalism and emotional intelligence

The role will occasionally require work outside standard hours, including evenings and weekends, around key campaign moments and releases.

RESPONSIBILITIES

From the conception of projects, work closely with artists, managers, A&R and General Manager to craft campaign strategies and release plans in line with the artists’ creative vision

Responsible for taking day-to-day ownership of assigned campaigns, ensuring that necessary information and assets are clearly communicated to all relevant teams; directing those teams to translate devised strategies into clear action to effectively deliver the campaign

Working with and bringing together input from A&R, Creative, Press, Digital, Marketing, Radio, Streaming, Retail & International teams to help determine priorities and campaign direction

Develop and manage detailed campaign timelines, identifying key milestones and opportunities across the release cycle (incl. promo / press trips)

Being the accessible “point person” for assigned projects day-to-day concerns; utilising excellent judgement in independently troubleshooting through issues or escalating as appropriate

Build and maintain trusted relationships with artists, managers, booking agents and other key external partners & being a reliable and accessible day-to-day point person for assigned artists and their core teams

Lead the coordination of campaign assets (artwork, press photos, videos & other creative assets) in collaboration with artists/managers, A&R and creative teams to ensure cohesive visual campaign strategies are achieved across marketing and promotion. Ensure all delivery deadlines are met.

Work closely with Beggars Group’s global teams to coordinate international campaign activity and maximise bespoke opportunities across key markets tailored to each campaign; ensuring teams are clearly briefed and equipped to support local campaigns effectively

Manage campaign budgets set in collaboration with the General Manager; track campaign spend and flag any changes in scope as they arise

Provide campaign specific updates, reporting, feedback, and ideas to key label and group stakeholders related to assigned campaigns

HOW TO APPLY

Applications close 6pm (UK time) on October 23. The role requires that you have the right to work in the UK indefinitely.
